user.description: Press the cap to wake it, then pick it from the list.

data_description.address: Caps heard in the last few seconds. The name ends with the number shown in the Żappka app.

gestures.title: Gestures
gestures.description: Press and long press already work. Turn on anything else you'll use with {name}: you can change it later in *Configure*.

abort.already_configured: This cap is already set up
abort.already_in_progress: This cap is already being set up
abort.no_devices_found: No awake Triki found. Press the cap and try again. If the Żappka app is open on a phone nearby, close it first: the cap takes one connection at a time.
abort.no_connectable_receiver: Home Assistant has no Bluetooth receiver that can connect to the cap. Add a Bluetooth adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy with active connections, then try again.
abort.heard_not_connectable: A Triki is in range, but only a receiver that can't connect hears it. Put a Bluetooth adapter or an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy with active connections (active: true) near the cap.

data_description.shake: Off by default. A few quick back-and-forth flicks of the wrist. The card's Check shows whether it also fires when you just pick the cap up.
data_description.tilt: Off by default. Hold the cap level, dot above the Z towards you (the yellow stripe on the card's model), and lean it right (tilt_right) or left (tilt_left) by 25° to 80°: one event, then another every 0.4 s while you hold the lean (repeat: true). Level it before the next lean. It's separate from the knob, so picking up the cap doesn't move a knob dimmer.
data_description.knob: Off by default. Turning the cap as it lies on the table sends rotate_cw / rotate_ccw, one event per knob step.
data_description.motion_gestures: Off by default. Tap, toss and flip, tuned on a single hardware session.
data_description.multi_press: Off: a press is reported as soon as you let go. On: each press waits out the window below to tell single, double and triple apart.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Timing, link and debug. The defaults suit most caps; the card's Check suggests a change when one is needed.

data.wake_as_press: Count the wake-up as a press

data_description.multi_press_window: The longest pause between letting go and pressing again that still counts as a double or triple press. Single presses are reported this long after you let go.
data_description.knob_step: How far you turn the cap on the table for one rotate event. 30° gives 12 events per full turn; smaller steps can flood slow lights.
data_description.invert_rotation: Swaps rotate_cw and rotate_ccw, for a cap used upside down or a dimmer that feels backwards.
data_description.wake_as_press: On by default. Only a press wakes the cap, so the press that woke it arrives as press (with source: wake) right after wake. It's skipped when the cap hadn't really slept, for example after a Home Assistant restart or a dropped link, so nothing toggles by itself. Turn this off if your automations already use wake to catch the first press.
data_description.sample_rate: Higher means snappier gestures and faster battery drain. Above 104 Hz, BLE often can't keep up.
data_description.idle_timeout: After this long with no motion or presses, the stream slows to 26 Hz but the link stays up, so presses still work. Any activity brings back the full rate.
data_description.sleep_timeout: After this long with no activity, the link drops. The cap then advertises for about 3 minutes before it sleeps, and presses don't register until it has slept; a press in between restarts the 3 minutes (the Readiness sensor shows this). 0 keeps the cap awake around the clock, which drains a CR2032 in about a week; at 30 % battery or less, 0 acts as 300.
data_description.capture: Each connection writes a .jsonl file with raw BLE notifications and detected events. Turn it off when you're done.

asleep.message: {name} isn't connected. Press it to wake it; if it is dozing off after an idle disconnect, wait about 3 minutes first.

confirm.title: Let {name} sleep between uses
confirm.description:
*Disconnect after idle* is 0, so the link never drops and the cap never sleeps. That draws about 1 mA: a fresh CR2032 lasts about a week, and a weak cell can lock the cap up until you take the cell out.

Submit to disconnect after {seconds} s without activity. Once the cap has slept, the first press wakes it and the link is back within a second or so.

battery_low.title: {name}: replace the battery
battery_low.description: The CR2032 in {name} measured {level} % at rest. A weak cell sags when the radio transmits and can lock the cap up: it stops advertising and presses do nothing until the cell is taken out. Replace it; this notice clears once a fresh cell is measured.

not_responding.title: {name} stopped responding
not_responding.description:
The link to {name} dropped on its own, and the cap hasn't been heard since. A healthy cap keeps advertising for about three minutes after a drop.

Press it once next to the Bluetooth receiver. If nothing happens, it has locked up: take the CR2032 out for a few seconds and put it back. This happens with a weak cell (last measured: {level}), so fit a new one rather than reuse it.

This notice clears as soon as the cap is heard again.

link_lossy.title: {name} loses a lot of its stream
link_lossy.description:
Over the last {sessions} sessions in a row, {name} got less than 70 % of its motion frames through (last one: {pct} %, via {via}). On a link like this, gestures, the knob and tilt miss steps; presses suffer less.

Move the cap or the receiver closer, add an ESPHome Bluetooth proxy near where you use the cap, or lower *Sensor rate* to 26 (options, under *Advanced*; now {rate} Hz). The card's **Check** measures the link and suggests a rate.

This clears after a session in which 90 % or more gets through.

options.knob: Knob: turn it flat on the table
options.multi_press: Double and triple press (a single press then waits half a second)
options.tilt: Tilt: hold it level, lean right or left
